claude-s · type-film

claude-s: a brand film for the repo, made by its own skill

Make an original 15–20 s brand film for claude-s, the open-source video-skills repo. Use its real README copy, real skill names and real numbers, and a mark designed from scratch as canvas paths. Mix screen HUD typing sonified with typeCues, iso.js assembling the skills, and a logo lock-up. Score it with sfx.py in the no-music sonified-UI mode, with a gap before the hero word.

What the skill did

  • Took techniques, not shots, from 8 references: fframes and ryanvogel (HUD typing, scramble → resolve), hairline (line tiers), srushtiddesign (iso hull solids), Claude's Dashboards launch (data → world lift, silence before the payoff), gxjo_dev (shape-match single take), Trenchers (the held gap) and the prompt-motion gallery (banned list, stills gate, critic, loop closure).
  • Every number on screen is read from the repo at render time: the 9 skills and their SKILL.md line counts, and sfx.py's 52 sounds with each one's real waveform.
  • Seven devices no reference has. The typed line's pitches rise above it as a skyline. seek(t) runs on a red field over the film's own timeline. A contact sheet shows the film's own frames under render.mjs's still names. Sounds draw their real waveforms as they play. Each skill grows to its SKILL.md length. The skyline lowers into the mark, and the mark's record light becomes frame 0's caret, so the film loops exactly.
  • The mark is new: a 3×3 contact sheet of 16:9 frames with the record light on, drawn as canvas paths; it is the skyline of the 9 skills seen from above.
  • 3 critique rounds plus a fresh critic. They redesigned 4 shots that read as a reference's: the HUD word, the typed line, the pen catalogue and a spark hop. They also enlarged the proof numbers to 150 px, held the URL for over a second, and fixed subframe blur smearing live digits.
  • Rendered at 30 fps with --subframes 4 motion blur and a light screen look (bloom, a 1 px fringe, vignette, grain). The loop seam passes render.mjs --loopcheck.

Sound

  • No music. The bed is room tone (sfx.py's drone mode), mastered to −16 LUFS.
  • Each typed key is a thock one step up its word's ladder. The bars above the line are those exact pitches.
  • The cut to red lands ON a tick burst plus a thump. The scramble's ticks are timed from the picture's own constants. The Enter press itself is silent, because clicks get no sound.
  • In the sound list, each name that lights up plays itself. In the skyline, each skill lands with a clink one step up a pentatonic scale: foley for objects.
  • A dry swell stops dead, then 0.3 s of true silence (13 dB under the room tone), then the hero: a sub drop and a root-and-fifth sting. The URL's keys fall where the opening's rose.
